item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Oct 30, 2026
item.description: Bubble: Market Signal on the $1T semiconductor wipeout (Intel -29%, SOX -7%) and whether the AI bubble is finally bursting; NBC News on Alphabet's worst day ever (-$500B+) and bubble anxiety; Ed Zitron on Anthropic's $430B in uncancellable contracts and hyperscalers not disclosing AI revenues; Joe Blogs on correction vs. collapse and what to watch (capex, credit, supply chain). Supply/demand: Forbes on Anthropic's $1T data-center and chip spending plan through 2045; Milk Road on SK hynix/Samsung memory, the supply-demand imbalance through 2027-28, and Micron as a buy-the-dip; Market Signal's close on the tension between a strong physical buildout and compressing stock multiples. Watchlist: Schwab Network's NVDA bull v. bear at the 200-day moving average; TheStreet on buying chips on dips (NVDA, AMD, AVGO, TSMC, ASML); FinVid on Intel's Q4 guide-down, the memory shortage persisting through 2027, and why this memory cycle differs (hyperscaler-led demand).

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Oct 28, 2026
item.description: Bubble: Fireship asks whether the AI bubble just popped — circular financing, CoreWeave's 15% debt, and Anthropic's $100B IPO; the concentration case — 80% of OpenAI/Anthropic profits from 1% of customers, half of Nvidia revenue from 3% of clients; Tom Lee's counterweight — debt markets preventing a runaway boom and a $30T build vs $25T for mobile/roadways; FinVid's close — lab revenues as ROI proof and compute constrained through 2028. Supply/demand: Microsoft + Google's $96.6B quarterly capex, KLAC's record quarter, Vertive orders doubling, and SK Hynix HBM demand over 2x supply; Anthropic's S-1 cash, Meta's offerings and SpaceX's $40B GPU lease reassuring buildout capital, plus Nvidia's $3B into Meta's offering; the fundamental semi shortage — clean-room underinvestment through 2027-28 and the market pricing in disbelief. Watchlist: KLAC's Q1 FY2027 beat — $4.14B revenue (+29%), $1.22 EPS, record 46.1% operating margin, services $850M (+14%); SpaceX's $40B Nvidia GPU financing and its pivot to renting compute; SK Hynix HBM4 overtaking HBM3E, demand over supply through 2030, LTAs covering over 50% of 2027-28 capacity, Samsung earnings due Oct 29, Micron's Taiwan union talks, and Chinese giants seeking memory LTAs through 2035.

item.title: AI Stocks Daily — Oct 23, 2026
item.description: Bubble first: House of El on Anthropic's $80B H1 loss (mostly accounting, but real cash burn: $1.76 spent per $1 earned), Amazon's $92B paper gain on convertible notes, $518B of non-cancellable compute contracts, and CoreWeave's $50B debt the market now prices as troubled. Ed Zitron on the IMF warning, the bond market freaking out, rising CDS on Nvidia/Microsoft/Meta, and 45% of market value in nine companies. Internet Education on circular financing (Nvidia<->OpenAI, Oracle debt) and the capex explosion: Meta $72B to $130-145B, Amazon $128B to $220B. Dividend Talks: Tom Lee's buy case vs negative combined hyperscaler FCF, Meta capex +80% vs revenue +26%, rising default-protection costs. Then the bull pushback: Luke Lango says financing fears are overblown, CoreWeave won't blow up, semis at cheapest valuations. Supply/demand: Jensen Huang at GTC Berlin — neoclouds are a working-capital problem, not a demand problem; no 2029 memory glut. Lango: Anthropic's slowdown is OpenAI's market-share gain; combined ARR growth re-accelerating since July. Ben Horowitz: Jassy says Amazon is 'out of everything' beyond 2028; the world stays compute-constrained at least through 2028. Watchlist: Lam Research guided slightly above consensus and would have guided higher without supply-chain constraints (demand too strong). And Huang's bearish counterpoint on memory: Nvidia is 'open-minded' to Chinese suppliers (CXMT), a direct read-across for Micron.
